clue.text: Detect a vibration and proceed cautiously

definitions.meaning: to sense a tremor by touch, picking up a feeling through the body
to advance carefully and tentatively, testing each step as you go

explanation.surface: Someone senses a tremor underfoot and edges forward with care.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both groping forward by touch and acting tentatively in an unfamiliar situation.

clue.text: Be upstanding when iniquity is evident

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A moral exhortation to stand tall whenever wickedness shows itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is gross wickedness, a direct synonym for this noun.

clue.text: Fabric from 51

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ace is the one in a pack of cards, making up the extra one

explanation.surface: A textile apparently dating from 1951.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 51 is split as 50 plus 1: Roman L for fifty and ACE, the card that counts as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is a delicate openwork textile, so it is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Refusal to parade for Greek governor

parts.note: no is a word of refusal
to parade is to march in procession

explanation.surface: A Greek official declines to take part in a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomarch is the head of a nome or nomos, a provincial district in Greece.

clue.text: Springs up when fools appear

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: spas are mineral springs

explanation.surface: Simpletons leap to their feet when idiots arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sap is a gullible person, so saps are fools, a plural noun matching the plural clue word.

clue.text: A County Council accustomed to being indicted

parts.note: CC is the standard abbreviation for County Council, a British local authority
used to something means accustomed to it

explanation.surface: A local authority finds itself facing charges as a matter of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To be accused is to be formally charged with an offence, the sense of indicted.

clue.text: Sack soldier? He can go to blazes!

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job
a fighter is a combatant or soldier

explanation.surface: An angry boss dismisses a soldier and tells him where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to blazes' reads as a curse, but literally this person goes to fires.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the person who attends blazes is one whose job is putting out fires.

clue.text: Applying oil to joint is hard graft

indicators.note: applying one thing to another here places the oil after the joint

parts.note: the elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm
to grease something is to apply oil or lubricant to it

explanation.surface: Lubricating a stiff joint turns out to be laborious work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means vigorous physical effort, the same as hard graft, British slang for hard work.

clue.text: Charge for a poster

definitions.meaning: a charge for goods or services, an invoice
a placard or printed notice stuck up in public

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a printed advertisement costs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an invoice demanding payment and a public notice, as in 'stick no bills'.

clue.text: Wary about religious group detaining priest

parts.note: circum is the Latin prefix for around or about

indicators.note: a group detaining someone holds them inside, so one letter goes within the other word

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous about a cult that is holding a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detaining' puts P inside SECT to make SEPCT.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumspect means cautious and watchful, a synonym of wary.

clue.text: Nothing in the boozer offers any cheer

indicators.note: something found in these words is carried within their letters

explanation.surface: A gloomy pub gives its drinkers no joy at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'boozER Offers'; 'the' and 'any cheer' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is the figure for nothing, a direct synonym.

clue.text: To make it, a job-seeker needs concentration

definitions.text: To make it, a job-seeker needs
definitions.meaning: the formal request for a post that every job-seeker has to submit

explanation.surface: Advice that anyone hunting for work must focus hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal request for a job and sustained diligent effort.

clue.text: Dissident group of men perpetrating crime

parts.note: male means relating to men
a faction is a dissenting group within a larger body

explanation.surface: A breakaway gang of men is committing offences.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefaction is criminal wrongdoing, the act of committing crime.

clue.text: Pretend Carol is in agreement

indicators.note: one word is in another when its letters sit within it

parts.note: a pact is an agreement
a carol is a song, and a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Someone named Carol only pretends to go along with a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is a song, a LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To playact is to make believe or put on a show, so it means pretend.

clue.text: In Katharine's opinion, it's a very sweet wine

parts.note: 'to me' means in my view, so in her opinion is to her
Kay is a short form of Katharine

explanation.surface: A woman named Katharine judges a dessert wine to be very sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In someone's opinion' is TO plus their name, as in 'to Kay it seemed sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine from the Tokaj region.

clue.text: Proposing to provide a definition

definitions.meaning: intending or having in mind, as in proposing to go
the sense or significance of a word

explanation.surface: Someone offering to supply a dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the participle of 'to mean', intending, and the noun for a word's sense.

clue.text: I object to upstart youth getting a gong

parts.note: the pronoun I in its object form is me

indicators.note: in a down entry, starting up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a cocky young man has been given an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' reads as a protest but is grammar: the object case of I.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or decoration.

clue.text: The baron's son, Edward, is sharp as a knife

parts.note: the son of a baron is styled the Honourable, abbreviated Hon
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A nobleman's son called Edward has a keen mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A honed blade has been sharpened on a stone, so it is as sharp as a knife should be.

clue.text: Stagger back to take a sly look

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: A drunk lurches backwards and casts a crafty glance.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a sly, suggestive way.

clue.text: A loafer, maybe, needs small garden tool

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
a hoe is a garden tool for weeding

explanation.surface: A lazy idler apparently requires a little implement for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loafer' suggests an idle person; it is a slip-on footwear style.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is a type of slip-on footwear, so it is an example of this.

clue.text: Depressed about the Italian

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Depressed about the Italian' (5): SAD round LA gives the letters, but no word defines the answer; the definition seems cut off and no search found the full clue.

clue.text: He ceases producing cork

definitions.meaning: one who stops, read literally as a person who halts
a plug for the neck of a bottle

explanation.surface: A man who stops making bottle corks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both one who stops and a bung or plug such as a cork.

clue.text: Striking and stylish

definitions.meaning: hitting hard, as in ... against rocks

explanation.surface: A description of someone both eye-catching and elegant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both smashing against something and attractively bold and elegant.

clue.text: Benevolent society is cautious about it

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: chary means cautious or wary

explanation.surface: A charitable association is wary of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity is an organisation set up to help others, a benevolent society.

clue.text: Bounty was not a small ship

parts.note: something not small is large
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: The Bounty was apparently a large vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounty' recalls the famous mutiny ship, but means generosity here.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving, which is bounty in its sense of liberality.

clue.text: Carry infant with little energy

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E is the short form for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A tired parent hauls a small child about.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry something, usually something heavy.

clue.text: The food is reasonable, they say

indicators.note: what they say is heard, so the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: fair means reasonable or just

explanation.surface: A diner judges the meal to be acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is the food served, as in good plain fare.

clue.text: Fellow and I see pastry being made

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A man and I watch dough being prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Filo is a paper-thin pastry used in Greek and Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: As soon as you get 1÷ 100

indicators.note: the division sign shows one word divided, split open by the other

parts.note: one is the number written out
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A sum: dividing one by a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The division sign is read literally: ONE divided by C, split as ON-C-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Once is a conjunction meaning as soon as, as in once you arrive.

clue.text: They appear to be phantoms

explanation.surface: A statement that ghosts appear as phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both things that appear and ghostly figures.

clue.text: Outside broadcast of old European instrument

parts.note: OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for outside broadcast

explanation.surface: A broadcast from location featuring an antique European musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: New food trader-and another

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
a grocer is a trader in food

explanation.surface: A novice shopkeeper selling food, and a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds a new food trader, and 'another' defines the answer as a further kind of food trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengrocer sells fruit and vegetables, so it is another kind of food trader besides the grocer.
